capabilityMatrix.note: The browser artifact builds the upstream qpdf executable rather than reimplementing PDF operations in JavaScript.
Chromium smoke validates a deterministic one-page PDF fixture and performs a real PDF rewrite.
The release smoke rewrites the deterministic one-page fixture with --linearize and validates the result.
QPDF's built-in native crypto provider is compiled without OpenSSL/GnuTLS.
Browser execution stages explicit files in Emscripten MEMFS.
QPDF browser-full is single-threaded and does not require cross-origin isolation.

notes: qpdf-v0.1.0 is the reviewed first package-release contract: browser-full, corresponding source/build recipe, standalone provenance/SBOM and SHA-256 checksums are produced only after the real Chromium smoke gate passes.
The build consumes the official qpdf-12.4.1.tar.gz release asset and verifies its GitHub-published SHA-256 before extraction.
The reviewed v12.4.1 annotated tag peels to exact upstream commit c37f83ae468abb6cc741f43b2f6fdeb66e550ffb.

The browser build uses QPDF's built-in native crypto provider, Emscripten zlib 1.3.2/libjpeg 9f ports and wasm-native exception handling; the release source bundle also carries the exact port sources and immutable Emscripten recipe snapshots.
The public Playground stages only checksum-verified qpdf-v0.1.0 assets and performs all PDF processing locally in a fresh Worker.
npm publication and automatic upstream candidate/promotion remain disabled until separately reviewed.

integration.summary: Self-host qpdf-core.js/qpdf-core.wasm plus the Zoo wrapper, then execute normal qpdf CLI arguments against PDF files staged in browser MEMFS.
notes: Use immutable qpdf-v0.1.0 release assets. The public Playground stages only checksum-verified files from that release.
Inputs and outputs are explicit browser-local MEMFS paths. Native host filesystem access is not exposed.
The wrapper preserves the upstream qpdf CLI and runs each invocation in a fresh Worker.
No SharedArrayBuffer or cross-origin isolation is required.
